title: Sensor-Modality-Aware Human Activity Recognition with the Convolutional Tsetlin Machine: Interpretable and Resource-Efficient Neuro-Symbolic Learning
new_feature: Applies a 2D Convolutional TM to raw UCI-HAR inertial windows (9x128) with quantile thermometer Booleanization, studies patch size/Booleanization granularity and decomposes sensor modalities (sensor, signal group, axis) to measure each modality's contribution; reports CPU and Arduino UNO Q (Cortex-A53) timing and memory footprint plus clause visualization.

datasets.name_in_paper: UCI Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones (UCI-HAR), raw inertial signals
datasets.input_shape_or_features: 9 channels x 128 samples raw inertial windows (body_acc, total_acc, body_gyro xyz); 561 precomputed features NOT used
datasets.split_as_reported: original UCI-HAR subject-independent split, 7352 train / 2947 test; for tuning, 20% of the training set held out as subject-disjoint validation (80/20)
datasets.booleanization: single threshold per channel (training-set mean) or B quantile thresholds per channel with thermometer encoding (best: 4 thresholds = 5 bins)
datasets.notes: 30 subjects, 50 Hz, 2.56 s windows with 50% overlap.

extraction_notes: Filename says 2025 but the article was published July 2026 (Sensors 26, 4482). Table 2 entries are means of 5 runs; Table 3 CTM row is the best run (95.11% in Table 4 caption, 0.951 in Table 3). Table 3 baselines were re-implemented by the authors on raw signals; the 'reported accuracy' column is from the original papers. Table 5 (25 modality subsets) reduced to the top-4, the three-axis single sensors and best/worst single channels; Table 6 activity-wise F1 and Table 2 per-activity accuracies omitted. code_url is the library used (cair/pyTsetlinMachineParallel), not paper-specific code.
